verses.text: Sarai, Abram's wife, had not given him any children. But she had an Egyptian slave woman named Hagar.
So Sarai said to Abram, "The LORD has kept me from having children. Go and sleep with my slave. Perhaps I can have a family through her." Abram agreed to what Sarai said.
So after Abram had been living in Canaan for ten years, his wife Sarai took her Egyptian slave Hagar and gave her to her husband to be his wife.
Abram slept with Hagar, and she became pregnant. When Hagar knew she was pregnant, she began to look down on Sarai.
Then Sarai said to Abram, "This wrong done to me is your fault. I put my slave in your arms, and now that she knows she is pregnant, she looks down on me. May the LORD judge between you and me."
Abram said to Sarai, "She is your slave, and she is in your power. Do with her whatever you think best." Then Sarai treated Hagar so badly that she ran away from her.
The angel of the LORD found Hagar near a spring of water in the desert. It was the spring beside the road to Shur.
He said, "Hagar, slave of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?" She answered, "I am running away from my mistress Sarai."
Then the angel of the LORD told her, "Go back to your mistress and obey her."
The angel of the LORD also said, "I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them."
The angel of the LORD went on, "You are pregnant, and you will have a son. You must name him Ishmael, which means 'God hears', because the LORD has heard about your suffering.
He will be like a wild donkey of a man. He will fight against everyone, and everyone will fight against him. He will live at odds with all his brothers."
Hagar gave this name to the LORD who spoke to her: "You are the God who sees me." She said, "Have I really seen the One who sees me and stayed alive?"
That is why the well was called Beer Lahai Roi, which means "the well of the Living One who sees me". It is still there, between Kadesh and Bered.
So Hagar gave Abram a son, and Abram named his son Ishmael.
Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael.
